text:
Jordan: quick sync  I sketched a minimal control-plane + data-plane contract for multi-region. Goal: a narrow surface to avoid future breakage. Link: https://redwood/internal/drive/multiregion/minimal_contract.png
Maya: nice. main questions: strong leases? audit fanout? client header semantics?
Jordan: proposal: 1) Leases are strongly consistent per-tenant (single-writer). 2) Client header: X-Redwood-Affinity: prefer-local | require-local. 3) Audit fanout must respect tenant.residency; no raw payloads cross-region unless consent=true.
Liam: proto sketch for lease (tiny):
```
rpc AcquireLease(tenant_id, preferred_site, ttl_ms, idempotency_key) -> (holder_site, expires_at_ms, lease_token)
```
Retries must be idempotent.
Sara: for residency tenants, AcquireLease must verify allowed_sites list and return 451+info header if outside set. Add an operator-runbook step to block automated failovers for these tenants.
Nina: observability: add attributes span.site and span.tenant_residency. metric: cross_site_failover{tenant,from,to,reason}. Keep label cardinality low by sampling.
Ethan: operational behavior: overloaded site -> if tenant.require_local -> return 429 + X-Redwood-RouteHint; else failover to next candidate. Preflight: no migrations in last 15m before cutover.
Maya: cache warming: async prefetch for top prefixes on steady-state affinity shift. Residency tenants only get consent-stamps (no raw prefetch).
Jordan: tests: (A) site kill: ensure residency tenants never cross-boundary; (B) surge: verify circuits and route hints; (C) leader-loss: assert no split-primary. I'll draft RFC with proto, runbook snippets, and test matrix. Tagging owners for review.
ops-bot: [policy] created gate `no_migrations_last_15m` for cutover preparations.
